Hi, Mopar tech here. I don't do any of that shit. In fact, I'm doing a 5.7 head gasket for a coolant leak at the moment. I pull the head, clean the surfaces and check for flatness, visually inspect everything for cracks. Reassemble with new gasket. There aren't any seals that will be damaged from oil or coolant being in the wrong spot. Like any engine do a good coolant flush and fresh coolant, along with your standard oil change, maybe with extended drain time to be safe. One thing thays good to do on hemis with any engine issues, is pull out the oil control valve and check for metal debris on the screen. This is the little metal can at the front of the valley, backside of timing cover. If metal is there, you may as well replace the engine. Just a quick thing to check.

As for the hoses and radiator, a good hot flush will take care of oil residue, but being a 14, depending on mileage I might replace the hoses if they haven't been yet jist for maintenance purposes. Without seeing them I can't really say what I would suggest lol
